sed: sed (conj.) — but; sed enim, but indeed
sedesque: sēdēs, sēdis (f.) — seat, abode, settlement (acc. pl.) + -que 'and'
sedet: sedeō, sedēre, sēdī — to sit (3rd sg. pres.) · also impers., it is fixed, resolved (+ dat.)
sequitur: sequor, sequī, secūtus sum — to follow, come after (3rd sg. pres. of deponent)
sic: sīc (adv.) — so, thus, in this way
sidera: sīdus, sīderis (n.) — star, constellation; pl. the sky (acc./nom. pl.)
simillima: similis, -e — like, similar (+ dat.); superl. simillimus (f. nom. sg.)
simul: simul (adv.) — at the same time, together
sint: sum, esse, fuī — to be (3rd pl. pres. subj.)
sistam: sistō, -ere, stitī, statum — to set, place, stand (1st sg. fut.)
soli: sōlus, -a, -um — alone, only (m. nom. pl.; gen./dat. sg. sōlī)
stant: stō, stāre, stetī, statum — to stand, stand firm (3rd pl. pres.)
sua: suus, -a, -um — his, her, its, their own (f. nom./abl. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
subtrahe: subtrahō, -ere, -traxī, -tractum — to withdraw, draw away (2nd sg. imper.; ne subtrahe, do not withdraw)
sui: suī (reflexive pron.) — of himself, herself, itself, themselves (gen. sg./pl.)
suis: suus, -a, -um — his/her/its/their own (m./f./n. abl. pl.; also dat. pl.) · sūs, suis — pig (dat./abl. pl., rare)
summa: summus, -a, -um — highest, topmost; surface of (f. abl. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.) · also f. nom. sg. (rēs summa; summa diēs)
suorum: suus, -a, -um — his, her, their own; suī (m. pl.) one's own people (m. gen. pl.; also n. gen. pl.)
suspicit: suspiciō, -ere, suspexī, suspectum — to look up at, gaze up at (3rd sg. pres.)
suum: sūs, suis (m./f.) — pig, boar, swine (gen. pl., = suum; not suus); also suus, -a, -um, his/her own (m. acc./n. nom./acc. sg.)
tandem: tandem (adv.) — at length, finally; in questions, pray, I ask
tellure: tellūs, tellūris (f.) — earth, ground, land (abl. sg.)
tempora: tempus, temporis (n.) — time, season, occasion (acc. pl.) · also tempora, -um (n. pl.), temples of the head (acc. pl.)
tendere: tendō, -ere, tetendī, tentum — to stretch, direct one's course, make for (pres. inf.)
terra: terra, -ae (f.) — land, earth, ground (nom./abl. sg.) · also f. voc. sg. (ō terra hospita)
testatur: testor, -ārī, -ātus sum — to call to witness, attest, swear by (dep.) (3rd sg. pres.)
tetendit: tendō, -ere, tetendī, tentum — to stretch, hold out, extend (3rd sg. perf.)
teucri: Teucer, Teucrī (m.) — Teucer, early king of Troy (gen. sg.) · also Teucrī, -ōrum (m. pl.) Trojans (voc. pl.: Teucrī, secludite) · also m. nom. pl. (Teucrī, Trojans)
tibi: tū, tuī — you (sg.); tibi, to/for you (dat.)
toros: torus, -ī (m.) — couch, bed; dining-couch, raised bank (acc. pl.)
tramite: trāmes, -itis (m.) — footpath, byway, track, course (abl. sg.)
tristis: tristis, -e — sad, grim, gloomy (m./f. nom. sg.; acc. pl. in -is = -ēs)
troiae: Trōia, -ae (f.) — Troy (gen. sg.) · also dat. sg., for Troy (sīc fāta ferēbant)
tua: tuus, -a, -um — your, yours (sg. poss.) (f. nom. sg.) · also n. acc. pl. (tua nūmina) · also f. abl. sg. (tua laude)
tuaque: tuus, -a, -um — your, yours (sg.) (f. abl. sg., with dextrā) + -que 'and' · also n. acc. pl. (tuaque arma) + -que
tueri: tueor, tuērī, tuitus sum — to watch, guard, protect (pres. inf., deponent)
tulit: ferō, ferre, tulī, lātum — to bear, bring, carry; sē ferre, to betake oneself (3rd sg. perf.)
utrasque: uterque, utraque, utrumque — each of two, both (f. acc. pl.; utrāsque palmās)
venimus: veniō, -īre, vēnī, ventum — to come (1st pl. perf., vēnimus; pres. venīmus)
vicit: vincō, vincere, vīcī, victum — to conquer, overcome (3rd sg. perf.)
videt: videō, vidēre, vīdī, vīsum — to see, behold (3rd sg. pres.)
virum: vir, virī (m.) — man, hero (acc. sg.; also gen. pl., old form = virōrum)
vita: vīta, -ae (f.) — life, living; the breath of life (nom. sg.; also abl. sg.)
vitta: vitta, -ae (f.) — fillet, headband, ribbon (abl. sg.; also nom. sg.)
vivis: vīvus, -a, -um — living, alive; vīvī, the living (m. dat./abl. pl.; also f./n.)
voces: vōx, vōcis (f.) — voice, word, utterance (acc. pl.; also nom. pl.)
volucrique: volucer, -cris, -cre — winged, swift, fleeting (m./n. dat./abl. sg.) + -que, and · also f. dat./abl. sg. (volucrī sagittā)
voluntas: voluntās, -ātis (f.) — will, wish, purpose, resolve (nom. sg.)
volvitur: volvō, volvere, volvī, volūtum — to roll, tumble (3rd sg. pres. pass.)
volvunt: volvō, volvere, volvī, volūtum — to roll, turn (3rd pl. pres.)
vos: tū, vōs — you (2nd pers. pl. pron.) (nom./acc. pl.) · also voc. pl. (vōs, aetērnī ignēs)
vox: vōx, vōcis (f.) — voice, word, sound (nom. sg.)
